instruction: Write a JavaScript function flatten(arr) that flattens a arbitrarily nested array of arrays into a single-level array, without using Array.flat.
Write a JavaScript groupBy(arr, keyFn) that groups items into an object whose keys come from keyFn(item) and values are arrays of items.
Write a JavaScript deepClone(obj) that recursively clones plain objects and arrays without using structuredClone or JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()).
Write a JavaScript unique(arr) that removes duplicates while preserving the first occurrence order.
Write a JavaScript minBy(arr, keyFn) and maxBy(arr, keyFn) that return the item with the smallest/largest key value.
Write a JavaScript rotate(arr, n) that rotates an array to the left by n positions (supporting negative n for right rotation).
Write a JavaScript chunk(arr, size) that splits an array into groups of the given size, with the last chunk holding any remainder.
Write a JavaScript pick(obj, keys) and omit(obj, keys) pair that return shallow copies with only/without the given keys.
Write a JavaScript invert(obj) that swaps keys and values of an object whose values are all strings or numbers.
Write a JavaScript frequency(arr) that returns an object counting how many times each value appears.
Write a JavaScript difference(a, b) returning values present in a but not in b.
Write a JavaScript sortByMulti(arr, keys) that sorts objects by multiple keys in priority order, e.g. by dept then name.
Write a JavaScript zip(a, b) that pairs elements of two arrays into an array of tuples, stopping at the shorter array.
Write a JavaScript transpose(matrix) that converts rows into columns for a rectangular 2D array.
Write a JavaScript get(obj, path, defaultValue) that reads a nested value by a path string like "a.b[0].c", returning defaultValue when missing.
Write a JavaScript setDefaults(obj, defaults) that returns a new object where missing keys are filled from defaults, without mutating the input.
Write a JavaScript swap([a, b]) style code that swaps two variables using destructuring, then swaps two object properties without a temp variable.
Write a JavaScript range(start, end, step) that generates an array of numbers like Python's range, supporting negative steps.
Write a JavaScript indexBy(arr, keyFn) that returns an object mapping each key to the last item with that key.
Write a JavaScript mergeDeep(target, source) that recursively merges nested plain objects, with source values winning on conflicts.
